narrative.overview:
The app is a student's desk: ruled index cards, a ballpoint pen and a lime highlighter. Ballpoint blue ink on white card stock, framed in ink rules, with one printed colour (the brand-stripe red) and one marker (the highlighter). Everything on the page is something a student actually uses to study; there is no metaphor to decode. Today is one index card: reviews, then writing, with the day's minutes marked in highlighter.

Headings are hand-lettered block caps, like a heading written at the top of a page of notes. Everything the student reads stays in Atkinson Hyperlegible. Surfaces are flat: depth comes from ink rules, not shadows. Panels are cut card with near-square corners, not pills.

Dark mode is the same card under a desk lamp at night: navy stock, pale ink, the stripe still red. Both schemes are first-class; dark follows the OS.
keyCharacteristics: Ballpoint blue text and rules on white stock; no Tailwind indigo.
One printed accent, red, for the current place only (the current tab and the stripe).
Hand-lettered caps for headings, Atkinson for all reading.
Ruling drawn per row, never behind text.

rules.name: The One Printed Colour Rule
rules.body: Red marks the current tab and the stripe. It is never a focus ring, a caret, a button fill, a link or decoration.

rules.name: The Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only signal. The current tab is also bold, carries aria-current="page" and gets a bar or stripe; errors carry "Error:"; layers and chart marks carry text labels.

rules.name: The Hand For Heads Rule
rules.body: .hand is for headings only, never for running text, labels, buttons or card content.

rules.name: The Dyslexia Override Rule
rules.body: Under the dyslexia option (OpenDyslexic, line-height 1.6), .hand turns off: OpenDyslexic 700, no caps, no letter spacing, no stroke. Headings keep their size.

rules.name: The Running Time Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures (tabular-nums) only on running times and Today's time, where digits line up in a column. Nowhere else.

rules.name: The Ruled Row Rule
rules.body: Ruling is drawn per row as a 1px rule-colour bottom border (.ruled), like the lines on an index card. Never paint ruling as a background behind text.

dos: Do use ink for text, frames and the primary fill; red only for the current tab and the stripe.
Do draw focus as a 4px double ink outline with a 2px offset.
Do frame panels as index cards (`.inlay`): white stock, 1.5px ink, 0.375rem corner.
Do draw ruling per row with `.ruled`.
Do set headings in `.hand` and everything read in Atkinson.
Do pair every colour signal with text, weight, shape or `aria-current`.

Do keep motion to state and one authored moment: colour transitions 150ms `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`; buttons press 1px down on `:active`; a new review or warm-up card slides in from the left (`.card-in`, 280ms clip-path reveal); revealing an answer turns the card over from its top edge (`.flip-in`, 380ms); "Right." / "Not quite." get an ink underline drawn under them (`.ink-draw`, 320ms); Today's highlighter strokes are laid on once. On every page the heading is written in by hand, left to right (`.hand-write`, a 560ms clip reveal of the words at a pen's steady pace), and its doubled ink rule is drawn under it (`.rule-draw`, 420ms, from 260ms) and the current tab's red mark is written in (`.mark-in`, 240ms); lists that arrive as lists (decks, essays, concepts, writing patterns, missed test questions) come in one row after another (`.track-in`, 260ms per row, 45ms apart, capped at the eighth row); triage and practice-test cards slide in like review cards; a practice-test score is stamped in with an ink underline. Selected test options ink their frame like review options. Background: three ruled index cards (`src/components/card-stack.tsx`), white stock in a 2px ink line at 22%, fanned on the desk in the right margin inside the app (1024px and up) and large beside the form on sign-in and password reset (onboarding shows it only from 768px: on phones its long form would scroll over the cards). They are dealt into the fan as each page opens (`.deal`, 560ms, 90ms apart), then stay still. A finished review squares the cards just reviewed into a small pile and draws a pen tick over it (`.pile`, `.tick`). In triage, a dragged card follows the finger and tilts; a kept card flies off to the right and a discarded one to the left while the next slides in. Pointing at or tabbing into a feedback card lays a highlighter stroke over its passage in the essay (`mark[data-linked]`, 320ms). Interactions: a button hover fills the key from the left with a 10% ink tint (220ms), link underlines press from 1px to 2.5px, a linked index card doubles its frame with an inset ink line, fields ink their border on hover and while typing. Honour reduced motion from the OS and the profile.
donts: Don't use red for focus, carets, links, buttons or decoration.
Don't use Tailwind indigo; the dark primary is night ballpoint with white text.
Don't add shadows or soft, pill-round panels.
Don't put metaphors on the desk. Every object and motion is something a student uses to study (index cards, pen, highlighter); the ground carries only the card stack.
Don't use the highlighter for anything but marking: Today's time, mastery strength and linked essay passages.
Don't set running text, labels or card content in the hand face.
Don't use tabular figures outside running times and Today's time.
Don't present writing time as an estimate.
